home.introHeading: Find a recovery meeting near you — free and anonymous
home.introBody: Fellow is a free, independent finder for recovery meetings across the United States — Alcoholics Anonymous (AA), Narcotics Anonymous (NA) and other 12-step and peer-support meetings. Search by city, day, or fellowship, browse the nationwide coverage map, or just tell Ask Fellow what you're looking for.

fellowship.safetyNote: A meeting is peer support, not medical care. If you've been drinking or using heavily for a long time, stopping suddenly can be risky — some withdrawal needs medical attention, and alcohol withdrawal in particular can be dangerous. If you feel unwell or unsafe, contact a doctor or your local emergency number.

fellowship.faqFreeA: Yes. {code} meetings are free to attend — no dues, fees, referral, or insurance needed — and anonymity is a core principle, so you can come as you are. Anyone who wants help is welcome.
fellowship.faqOnlineAHas: Yes. Fellow lists {online} online {code} meetings you can join from anywhere, alongside in-person groups near you.
fellowship.faqOnlineAFinder: Many {code} groups meet online as well as in person. The official {code} finder lists current online meetings.
fellowship.faqOnlineANoFinder: Many {code} groups meet online as well as in person. Each group's own website lists current online meetings.
fellowship.faqReligiousQ: Do I have to be religious to join {code}?
fellowship.faqReligiousA: No. {code} welcomes people of any religion or none. The program is usually described as spiritual rather than religious, and many areas offer secular, agnostic, or non-religious meetings.
fellowship.faqSpecificQ: Are there {code} meetings for specific groups, like women's or young people's?
fellowship.faqSpecificA: Often, yes. Larger areas hold meetings for specific communities — women's, men's, young people's, LGBTQ+, and newcomers' groups among them. Use Fellow's live search to filter for the meeting that fits.

about.p1: Fellow is a free, independent, non-commercial project that helps people find recovery meetings quickly — 12-step fellowships and related peer-support programs alike. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or a representative of Alcoholics Anonymous or any other fellowship, program, or service body. There are no accounts, no ads, and nothing to sign up for.
about.p2: There are two ways to find a meeting. Browse lets you type a place, ZIP, group, or a plain phrase like "Sunday morning AA near me," and filter by day, time, fellowship, and location — including a "Starts soon" view for meetings beginning shortly. Ask Fellow is a chat assistant you can talk to in your own words (for example, "my partner's drinking is a problem — is there something for me?"). Either way, you can open a meeting's details to get directions, add it to your calendar, or share it.
about.hSources: Where the meeting data comes from
about.sourcesLead: Meeting listings are aggregated from public feeds published by local 12-step intergroups and service bodies. We read them through two open community data standards:
about.tsmlDesc: — the "12 Step Meeting List" standard maintained by
about.tsmlDesc2: , used by A.A. and many other fellowships.
about.bmltDesc2: , used by Narcotics Anonymous and others.
about.sourcesOutro: The listings belong to those intergroups and fellowships, who do the real work of keeping them current. Fellow simply gathers them into one searchable place. If your intergroup would like its feed added, corrected, or removed, please get in touch.
about.includedLead: Fellow aims to cover 12-step fellowships and related peer-recovery programs that publish open meeting data, including:
about.includedNote: A few of these — such as Recovery Dharma, a mindfulness-based path — are not 12-step programs; they're included because they serve the same need and publish open meeting data. Coverage varies by area and grows over time — not every program publishes open data everywhere.
about.privacyLead: Anonymity and privacy are foundations of recovery, and Fellow is built to respect them. We don't ask who you are, we don't create accounts, and we don't track you across the web or run advertising.
about.privLocation: When you tap "Near me" or enter a ZIP code, your approximate location is used to sort meetings by distance. Those coordinates are sent to our search service and a mapping provider only to return nearby results — they are not stored by Fellow or linked to any identity.
about.privNoData: Fellow doesn't collect names, contact details, or a record of which meetings you view.
about.privChat1: To answer you, the messages you type — plus your approximate location, if you've shared it — are sent to our AI provider (
about.privChat2: ) to generate a reply and search for meetings. Fellow doesn't store your conversations or link them to you, and the assistant only shows real meetings from the index — it can't invent one. Please don't include identifying details; messages are processed under Anthropic's own policies.
about.privMaps: Opening a map, Street View, or directions hands off to Google Maps, which has its own terms and privacy policy.
about.accuracy: Meeting details change often, and public feeds can lag. Please treat listings as a helpful starting point and confirm with the group before you go — especially for a first visit. Spot something wrong, missing, or that should be taken down? Let us know and we'll fix it.
about.disclaimer: Fellow is provided "as is," without warranty of any kind. Fellowship names and marks belong to their respective organizations and are used here only to identify meetings. Fellow is an independent effort and does not speak for any fellowship.
